headline: Apple reports tonight as markets weigh Friday's chip rout; gold hovers near 52 week low
subhead: After Friday's 1.8 percent S&P 500 drop and 2.9 percent Nasdaq slide, OPEC+ held December output steady, gold rose 0.3 percent to 3,909 dollars, about 0.3 percent above its 52 week low, and Bitcoin held near 77,950 dollars.

us.text: The S&P 500 fell 1.8 percent to 7,580 and the Nasdaq 2.9 percent to 25,437 as chip stocks lost about 1 trillion dollars in value.
Intel fell 28.6 percent after guiding fourth quarter revenue to 15 to 16 billion dollars versus about 17 billion expected; Qualcomm fell 11.1 percent.
Apple reports fiscal fourth quarter results after the close on 2 November, guiding to 9 to 11 percent revenue growth, the first call led by CEO John Ternus.

india.text: The Nifty rose 0.5 percent to 23,053.10 and the Sensex 308 points to 74,459.53 on IT and pharma buying; Bank Nifty slipped 0.4 percent.
FIIs were net buyers of 3,598.54 crore rupees in cash on 30 October while DIIs sold a net 817.51 crore (provisional).
The rupee gained 33 paise to close at 94.93 per dollar on a weaker dollar and firmer local stocks.

global.text: Asian chip stocks led Friday's regional sell-off; early Monday the Nikkei was down 0.5 percent and the KOSPI 1.0 percent.
The STOXX 600 fell 0.4 percent to 646.75 and the DAX 0.9 percent, though Europe still logged its best month since June.
OPEC+ core members kept December output targets unchanged on 1 November; WTI was down 1.6 percent at 102.45 dollars in early trade.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on whether AI spending pays: Alphabet had its worst day on record after negative free cash flow, ServiceNow and Caterpillar sank on guidance, and Intel and Amazon closed the week with a broad tech sell-off that left the Nasdaq down 2.0 percent and the S&P 500 down 0.6 percent. The Fed held rates on 28 October with two officials favouring a hike, and with oil lifted by fresh Hormuz attacks, rate fears hit metals hardest: gold lost 2.5 percent on the week to near a 52 week low and silver 7.3 percent. India moved the other way, with the Nifty back above 23,000 on IT and pharma buying, Trent jumping on results and foreign investors turning net buyers on Friday. Crypto absorbed a 6.3 billion dollar Binance hack, leaving Bitcoin down 2.6 percent over the past week near 78,000 dollars. Next week brings Apple results on 2 November, the US midterm elections on 3 November, the Bank of England on 5 November and US payrolls on 6 November.
